questions.question_english: The rationale behind moving away from the strict "no-detention" policy to a discretionary "holding back" policy in 2019 was primarily due to:

Deteriorating learning levels and reduced academic accountability across states.

questions.explanation_english: The shift away from an absolute no-detention policy toward discretionary state-level holding back arose primarily due to concerns over falling learning outcomes, reduced student effort, and diminished academic accountability across states. questions.question_english: If a recognized private unaided school denies admission to a child belonging to a weaker section citing lack of financial compensation from the government in advance, what is the most appropriate administrative view as per the RTE Act?
options_english: The school is legally justified in delaying entry because state government reimbursement must precede admission.
The school should formally refer the child to a neighborhood government school that receives direct state grants.
The school violates Section 12(1)(c) by conditioning entry-level admission on financial reimbursement.
The school can demand a formal financial guarantee letter from the local authority prior to admitting the student.
questions.explanation_english: Section 12(1)(c) mandates that private unaided schools must admit at least twenty-five percent EWS and disadvantaged students at the entry level without imposing pre-conditions. Conditional delay or denial of admission pending government reimbursement violates statutory provisions, as public reimbursement mechanisms operate independently of the mandatory admission obligation established by the statutory legal framework governing universal elementary access.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर विकल्प C है। धारा 12(1)(ग) के अंतर्गत पात्र कमजोर वर्गों और वंचित समूहों के बच्चों को प्रवेश-स्तर पर प्रवेश देना विद्यालय का दायित्व है। प्रतिपूर्ति की प्रशासनिक प्रक्रिया को प्रवेश रोकने की शर्त नहीं बनाया जा सकता। विद्यालय को पहले वैधानिक प्रवेश-दायित्व का पालन करना चाहिए; प्रतिपूर्ति का दावा अधिनियम और नियमों के अनुसार अलग प्रक्रिया से निपटाया जाता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) The school violates Section 12(1)(c) by conditioning entry-level admission on financial reimbursement.

Section 12(1)(c) mandates that private unaided schools must admit at least twenty-five percent EWS and disadvantaged students at the entry level without imposing pre-conditions. Conditional delay or denial of admission pending government reimbursement violates statutory provisions, as public reimbursement mechanisms operate independently of the mandatory admission obligation established by the statutory legal framework governing universal elementary access.

questions.question_english: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009 derives its statutory basis primarily from which Constitutional provision introduced by the 86th Amendment Act?
options_english: Article 21A
Article 45
Article 51A(k)
Article 46
questions.explanation_english: Article 21A was added to the Constitution of India by the Eighty-Sixth Amendment Act in 2002. This constitutional framework serves as the primary legal foundation for enacting the statutory provisions of the Right to Education Act, 2009 across the nation.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर अनुच्छेद 21क है। 86वें संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 2002 ने 6 से 14 वर्ष की आयु के बच्चों के लिए निःशुल्क और अनिवार्य शिक्षा को मौलिक अधिकार बनाया। RTE अधिनियम, 2009 इसी संवैधानिक अधिकार को लागू करने के लिए विस्तृत वैधानिक व्यवस्था प्रदान करता है। अनुच्छेद 45 छह वर्ष से कम आयु के बच्चों की प्रारंभिक देखभाल और शिक्षा से संबंधित है, जबकि अनुच्छेद 46 कमजोर वर्गों के शैक्षिक और आर्थिक हितों को बढ़ावा देने से जुड़ा है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Article 21A

Article 21A was added to the Constitution of India by the Eighty-Sixth Amendment Act in 2002. This constitutional framework serves as the primary legal foundation for enacting the statutory provisions of the Right to Education Act, 2009 across the nation.
